svg.aria-label: Nine designs in five families: shared memory, shared nothing, shared key-value store, shared buffer pool, and shared disk, each drawn as one or two stacks of application, SQL, access methods, cache and disk. In every family but shared memory and shared disk, the left design lets the node that owns the data decide which transactions commit, and the right design moves that decision elsewhere. Shared disk storage never decides; its two designs differ in how many nodes do. Side-by-side boxes run on different nodes, spanning boxes are shared, and orange copies behind a box are replicas. Blue lines mark where nodes couple and what crosses; orange lines mark where data is copied and what is sent; dashed grey marks where concurrency control runs and who may write. In the deterministic design, Calvin, the orange line sits above the blue one: it copies its input log before it splits work among partitions.
svg.text: Where nodes couple, where data is copied, and who may write
Each family is named for what every node shares. Boxes side by side run on different nodes; a box spanning both is shared.
Blue: where nodes couple, and what crosses. Orange: where data is copied, and what each replica receives. Dashed grey: concurrency control, and who may write.
In each family with two designs, the left one lets the node that owns the data decide what commits, and the right one decides elsewhere. Shared disk is the exception: its storage never decides.

g.text: one writer per partition; locks in log order
any node writes; check at commit
